newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Balladur bond cost govt three bln Ffr - finm.
newsitem.headline: French Balladur bond cost govt three bln Ffr - finm.

text.p: France's so-called Balladur bond, named after former conservative prime minister Edouard Balladur, has cost the state a little over three billion francs excluding service charges, the finance ministry said on Wednesday.
The finance ministry said repayment of the bond required no exceptional measures and was covered by the government's regular debt issuance programme announced at the end of 1996.

Fiscal expenditures to facilitate the bond's placement cost about 2.2 billion francs given the tax exemption of capital gains from sales of mutual funds invested in the bonds and the exemption of interest paid when the bonds were held in share savings plans.
Placement commissions were on the order of 850 million francs.
